metadata.title: Wither
annotation: In many cases, depression comes without a defined catalyst and the sufferer of the disorder will try to rationalize their depression to a certain event or person.
Depression can cause people to change dramatically, to the point where they may not even recognize themselves.
There is a way for the writer to break free from depression; this could be taken as either committing suicide or taking the initiative to seek help.
Many depressed people sleep excessively. It is an activity in which they don’t have to think about their condition, and some argue that it simulates death.

2) **I’ve Passed This Way Before** - Jimmy Ruffin
    Another poignant song by Jimmy Ruffin, this track echoes the sentiment of history repeating itself and a heart being broken again. The valence (0.931) suggests a melancholic yet resilient mood.

3) **A Heartache For A Keepsake** - Faron Young
    This country tune shares your sentiments about heartache and loss, with lyrics such as "A heartache for a keepsake, what a tragic souvenir". The valence (0.855) indicates a slightly hopeful undertone despite the sadness.

4) **Gone** - We The Lion
    This folk song expresses feelings of loss and confusion, with lyrics like "I'm sorry for my screaming, I swear this isn't me behind this flesh". The valence (0.328) suggests a somber yet introspective mood.

5) **Brand On My Heart** - Willie Nelson
    This country ballad tells the story of a troubled heart and blame, with lyrics such as "My troubled old heart dear is beating with pain". The valence (0.237) indicates a deeply sad yet reflective mood.

metadata.title: What Becomes of the Brokenhearted
annotation: This line is an example of the literary trope called “rhetorical question.” A rhetorical question is a question that is asked for effect rather than to elicit an answer. The effect of this is to make the listener think.

The ending to this verse changed from “Maybe” to “Help me” –  a first step in recovery is reaching out for help.

This may explain the song’s purpose, a desperate call for  help in what is presented as a no win, fatalistic scenario.

A supposedly positive statement put into doubt but one last word.

The lyricist sounds quite decisive about doing “the right thing”, but then self doubts overcome with a devastating “Maybe”.

The song moves on like a swing, between despair and hope, darkness and light.

Often presented as a question – “Is happiness an illusion?” as in this discussion of a Ted Talk

Here it comes as a statement, to stress the depth of the narrator’s depression

From the talk –

Is it even possible to have a constant state of happiness or is being happy just a fleeting feeling that only lasts a few moments?

A common metaphor for lost hope, used extensively in literature and music lyrics.

The earliest known use of the term was in Al Dubin’s 1934 Boulevard of Broken Dreams –



In the modern era, Green Day used the same title for their 2004 hit.

In contrast to the fatalistic previous lines – “All is lost, there’s no place for beginning
All that’s left is an unhappy ending”, the last verse does talk about hope, determination to change course and break away from the downhill path of “broken dreams”.

Like many songs of the era, a version in Italian was recorded by Jimmy Ruffin, called “Se Decidi Cosi” – “So if You Decide” where the lyrics address the love object, while the original version has past this stage.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UbaeEE8q4Fk

The very long orchestral came to replace a spoken first verse that was deleted in the final cut. There are no other purely instrumental parts in the song.

The original spoken intro:

A world filled with love is a wonderful sight.
Being in love is one’s heart’s delight.
But that look of love isn’t on my face.
That enchanted feeling has been replaced.

A fitting intro to the following sad saga, establishing the contrast between the past and the present.

The extended original version –

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r-N-qMTxE0s

metadata.title: All I Know
annotation: Regardless of what they said to him he cannot escape the past. He still can hear their voice and cannot look at them without feeling sadness.
They also say that he should move on too. The past is gone and the only thing left to do, is to focus on the future.
He makes an attempt to confront his past. When he does they do not care, because they have moved on.
He still can hear their voice in his mind. Whenever he looks at them his heart fills up with his past feelings.
He again continues to try and let his past go, but he is so used to the comfort of being in a relationship.
He continues to try and let his past go, but he is so used to the comfort of being in a relationship.
He realizes that his relationship is over. However he is not prepared to accept it.
When you are with someone for so long it is hard to picture your life without them.

   This country song expresses a sense of disillusionment and dissatisfaction, as shown in the lyrics "There's no more flowers There's no more spring There's no more promises Of golden wedding rings." The somber tone will likely resonate with your feelings.

4) **My Love, My Illness, My End** - **Deadbeat Nightlife**
   This punk song addresses the feeling of being overwhelmed and hopeless, as suggested by the lyrics "Waking up to the reality that everything I do and everything I'll try is meaningless." The energetic sound will provide an outlet for your emotions.

5) **Fade To Black** - **Apoptygma Berzerk**
   This electronic track expresses feelings of despair and a desire to escape, as shown in the lyrics "Life it seems will fade away Drifting further every day Getting lost within myself Nothing matters, no one else I have lost the will to live Si..." The atmospheric sound will likely provide a fitting backdrop for your emotions.

metadata.title: Debris
annotation: When he was at his absolute best, people still thought he wasn’t good enough, and now that he isn’t at his best anymore, people like him even less.
Afraid of thoughts that keep coming back
He came with nothing to his name but the want to improve the person, but in the end, he couldn’t do anything of the sort.
This is stated as an optimistic thing, because he feels like he deserves what has been coming to him.
Talking about how everyone he’s ever been with has ended up leaving him, like a piece of garbage.

The person who’s being talked about isn’t truly there. The presence may be there, but their mind is somewhere else, wanting to be  anywhere but there. They’re compared to a carcass because they might as well just be a husk.

1) **Sinking** - **Jesus Piece**
   This song's raw, intense lyrics about feeling lost and empty resonate deeply with your sentiment. The heavy punk genre adds to the emotional weight of the track.

2) **I Can Hear My Heart Break** - **Conway Twitty**
   This classic country ballad captures a sense of loneliness and pain that matches your request. The lyrics about being surrounded by silence and tormented dreams are particularly poignant.

3) **Lucy’s Tale** - **Sarah Sparks**
   This folk song's melancholic tone and lyrics about restlessness, feeling out of place, and longing for a sense of belonging echo your feelings of being surrounded by pain.

4) **Offering of Fire** - **Lorna Shore**
   The metal genre and the song's dark, brooding atmosphere create an intense emotional landscape that mirrors your feelings of being in a dark place. Lyrics like "Troubled times we have fallen" also resonate with your sentiment.

5) **Standing Alone - Isolation** - **Vales**
   This punk track's title and lyrics about isolation, feeling disregarded by humanity, and dreaming in sunlight reflect the emotional state you described. The high-energy tempo adds a sense of urgency to the song.

annotation:
The man calls out to any supernatural or powerful being, and requests that his pain comes to an end. This will ultimately lead to more hardship, as revealed throughout “Flesh Coffin.”

https://genius.com/albums/Lorna-shore/Flesh-coffin

He wishes for no one to interrupt his attempt on his life, and is excited to finally be at peace. Unfortunately, he has eons to go before he can even think about peace. This is revealed throughout “Flesh Coffin.”

https://genius.com/albums/Lorna-shore/Flesh-coffin

The man feels trapped within his body, as if his soul were locked inside of a cage. He believes that suicide is the answer, and that his pain will fade after he is dead. This is revealed to be far from what will actually happen in the third track off the album, titled “The Astral Wake Of Time.”

metadata.title: Ragnarok
annotation: A repeat of the above motif.

The ‘Somewhere in Time’ motif, which appears throughout P2’s ‘Trilogy’ (Muramasa, Ragnarok, Masamune).

Here, it’s being clearly stated that humanity is becoming increasingly disconnected, and that this will ultimately be the cause of our downfall if we don’t act soon.

This line is also mentioned later in Masamune, although changed to “There’s 𝗻𝗼 pardon for a meddling soul.” Which makes sense as this is the halfway point of the album, and the first, middle, and third track share the “somewhere in time” motif.

metadata.title: Nerve
annotation: The speaker describes their state of mind as constantly aggravated or distressed. They feel as though they are always passing through life without being truly heard or understood by others.

The speaker describes severing a nerve, suggesting a desire to detach themselves from the neglect they have experienced from someone close to them. They use the imagery of thorns in the vein, reaching the brain, to express the influence of harmful or malicious intentions.
The speaker metaphorically places themselves outside the addressee’s house, feeling desperate or close to death.

metadata.title: Hall Beach
annotation: I interpret this as a commentary on trying to improve, in a community/subculture that is built on feeling bad.
She holds onto the words/compliments said to her as security when she cant be confident in herself.

She is the most stable she has ever been, but is still struggling as a young adult. She alludes here to (possibly) drunken nights and instability, a constant theme in this song; an unwillingness to take care of herself and/or take care of herself continuously.

metadata.title: Sweet Avenue
annotation: It’s been so long since Blake has felt alive, to the point where he felt he was dead inside. Then this person comes along and makes him feel alive again, and he explains that he was dying to feel this way once more.

In this line, Blake is stating how he wants to take things slow, and he wants his significant other to show him where the relationship (the train) is going to go, possibly because he loves this person to the point where he’d be happy with them no matter how the relationship went.

For the first time in his life he felt it was worth it to love someone, and for the first time he felt he deserved this person’s affection, it’s a pretty cool way to end such a depressing and pretty thought provoking album.

People say that when you fall for someone everything seems to look more beautiful and taste better, etc. Blake plays with this idea and says that his entire life is now better that he’s found someone he loves.

metadata.title: Miracle
annotation: In these verses, Sondae joyfuly declares his belief in the transformative power of the Holy Ghost, acknowledging that everything within him is poised to praise the Lord. The phrase “I’m standing in the presence of a miracle” suggests a profound awareness of the divine and the miraculous nature of this encounter. Sondae expresses a sense of sanctification through the acknowledgment of Christ’s sacrifice on the cross, and there’s a celebration of all creation joining in praise for the Lamb of God. This sentiment aligns with the biblical understanding of sanctification through Christ, found in passages like 1 Corinthians 6:11. The repeated use of “miracle” emphasizes the awe-inspiring nature of Sondae’s encounter with the divine.

In these verses, Sondae,  is sharing that even though he has many plans in his heart, he acknowledges that Jesus has the final say in everything. It’s like he’s recognizing Jesus as a source of comfort and light, especially in challenging times. The line “I can walk because You are the way” emphasizes Sondae’s reliance on Jesus as a guide and support in his journey. It echoes a similar sentiment found in Proverbs 19:21, which says, “Many are the plans in a person’s heart, but it is the Lord’s purpose that prevails.” This connection to biblical wisdom reflects Sondae’s understanding of surrendering his plans to Jesus and relying on Him as the ultimate guide in life.

This lyric references R. Kelly’s song named “Your Body’s Callin”.  R. Kelly wrote and produced this song and he decided to re-cycle it.

When you found that special someone you’re bound to know it. That person may bring happiness and love into your life that maybe hasn’t been there in a while. This person may motivate you to be a better you than you were yesterday. So, when this person does come into your life you make it a priority that you tell them how much of a blessing they are.

metadata.title: Acid Again
annotation: WNEW reporter Steve Young recorded his interview with a young lady who was strung out on drugs and released it on vinyl as “A Child Again.”
Originally identified only as “A Hippy Named Marcy,” in 2011 Bruce Porter tracked down the original interviewee and found that her real name was Margaret Bachman.

4) **Weight** - **Stuck Out**

metadata.title: Afraid
annotation:
Although Jesse could be worried about other people having the same fears as he does, he’s more likely expressing a fear about not being authentic anymore.

These lines aren’t literally meant, they imply an unawareness for the changes to his personality, which cause him to become unauthentic. In that sense, to wake up means to realise this difference.

All day, Jesse walks around frightened to do anything. His only source of comfort is his relationship, but even that is one of his biggest causes for stress. Using sleep as an extended metaphor throughout the song, he asks his girlfriend to release him from her tormenting grasp, and give him a peaceful rest and wake up.

Even when he’s sleeping, he’s vulnerable to showing his weaknesses and insecurities, but wants his friends to ignore their findings. Now, he’s lacking in a faith in anything, a point addressed on the first song on the album, “How”.

Even with the turmoil that goes on in the relationship, Jesse advises himself to keep on with his life, and not to completely detach himself, only suggesting to sell his soul, and not his body and mind.
While his friends are telling him that his relationship is fine, Jesse knows that internally, they’re actually thinking that it’s on the rocks and on the way out soon.
Even though she’s putting on a happy face, Jesse can tell that internally, she’s about to begin making things hard on him again.

After his girlfriend pesters him to the point of feeling sick, Jesse understands that she’s constantly going back-and-forth with being satisfied.

He is constantly going up and down with his  feelings about his career, relationship, and future. He’s plagued with the thought that he could lose his life and livelihood to “the next big thing”.

He seems to be talking about himself (and maybe creating an insight into the future of his career) throughout the entire song. If you watch the music video, there is no girl at any instance. Near the end, the blinking eye that has served as a frame up until this point zooms out and reveals to be his own eye. Jesse has been watching everything that was happening, because he just woke up, and he saw himself. This song is not about a romantic relationship as many people have interpreted it to be — it is about Jesse’s future. But ultimately this song can be understood in many contexts, this just seems like the intended one.
This message of insecurity opens up the song, setting the tone for the lyrics to follow. The spacey feel of the intro makes it seem as if he’s just woken up, with this fear possibly being realized.

metadata.title: Panic Attack
annotation: the Lack of a Rhyme in this chorus could be some form of leaving the listener hanging, and not resolving the chorus before moving into the refrain

Panic attacks will trigger the body’s Fight-or-Flight response, this is worded in a question as during a panic attack where there is no clear or present danger, the mind and/or body will not know if this is a fight or a flight situation.

“Why do I feel so numb?” is a question many with panic disorders may ask, why do I feel this way? What is wrong with me? The narrator is trying to assess why these feelings are occuring with no answer.
Sometimes one can sense a panic attack oncoming from a heightened sense of nervousness or feeling fear randomly, threatening to push you over the edge.

Having a panic disorder causes frequent panic attacks which can be seen as “bouts of fear” the narrator stating that it “permeates all he sees” cause be that many with panic disorder often fear their next panic attack so fear can permeate your whole life or everything you see as you fear the next onset of an attack.

When one suffers from panic disorder they have frequent panic attacks which can make sleep difficult because you can suffer panic attacks in your sleep, awakening you (or disturbing your sleep as it were), leaving your mind restless.
A common complaint of anxiety and panic disorder patients is a feeling of being overwhelmed, and being unable to focus or concentrate, as if in a delirium state.

Panic attacks activate the body’s “fight or flight” response, as mentioned earlier in the song. In this particular instance, the character seems to have decided to try and run and hide from whatever induced the panic attack. If the character is indeed suffering from Panic Disorder, then this will be a futile attempt, as panic attacks caused by this disorder do not have triggers; objects, occurrences, etc. that set off a panic attack (like in a phobia) and so are unable to be run away from.
Sufferers of Panic Disorder often feel very anxious and scared, living in fear that another panic attack will occur.

Panic Disorder itself is not marked by any specific phobia, but victims of it often suffer from Agoraphobia in tandem with it, which is a phobia denoted as a fear of going out into a public place (at least, it takes that form most often; it takes other forms as well) due to the fear that they will have a panic attack while in a public place, embarrassing themselves as well as anyone they might happen to be with.

Those suffering from a panic attack often feel as if they will die at any moment, making them feel as if they are in urgent need of medical attention. Of course, this is a false sense as oftentimes, people suffering from panic disorder don’t have many other health issues and any they do have are not usually life-threatening, making this feeling of urgency unneeded.
People in the middle of a panic attack are unable to think clearly, and so fall into a state of hysteria, not knowing what to do, what’s happening, or how to fix it.

Often times, sufferers of Panic Disorder will have lingering anxiety after an attack and constantly live in fear of another attack happening, and this causes them to be very tense (often times to the point of having aches, pains, and lingering tension in their muscles). During a panic attack, the sufferer may feel as if they can’t get enough air, hence the feeling of being choked. Of course, this is a very worrisome state to be in, and the anxiety of having another panic attack would also leave the sufferer in a constant state of worry.

The character is experiencing more symptoms associated with a panic attack. In particular, this section is talking about the sudden appearance of the panic attack and that there are never any warnings present as to when a panic attack is going to happen. This pushes the character’s condition towards Panic Disorder, a disorder marked by the onset of random, non-trigger panic attacks for seemingly no reason with no warning whatsoever.

Simply put, a very rough outline of some of the symptoms associated with a panic attack. This one, in particular, seems rather intense, he’s effectively lost control over himself emotional and partially physically. It even gets to a point where the narrator gives up on trying to fix the issue, possibly indicating suicidal thoughts.

The instrumental breakdown starting at the beginning here changes, perhaps indicating the onset of these symptoms.

Fitting in the song title, panic attacks are often characterized by sudden bouts of anxiety that are usually not identifiable in origin. What exactly is making me so nervous? A person with panic disorder often has difficulty answering this question.

This characteristic is often what makes panic attacks not so easily treated by advice. Being told to “calm dowm” or “relax” rarely works for a person undergoing a panic attack. A person might want to be calm and collected, but when the attack occurs, the sensations are involuntary. Depending on the degree of attack intensity, it can be socially and physically debilitating.

Panic attacks often make you feel like your life is in danger, thus your brain makes you think you’re dying. And they often freeze your brain from thinking rationally.

Your body produces epinephrine (colloquially known as adrenaline) in response to a perceived but nonexistent threat. Your mind can’t locate the threat, so it produces more epinephrine. Chest pain, palpitations, a pounding and racing heart, sweatiness, intense fear, and shaking can give the affected person the impression that they are dying.

The song begins by alternating between two different time signatures to set up a panicked, almost unnerving feel to the song. James LaBrie describes an unnamed character’s sudden onslaught of symptoms while trapped inside a panic attack.

metadata.title: PANIC ATTACK
annotation: This translates to “Fear creeps up on us again / Help me make it go away” in English. So, the speaker is saying that this panic attack is not the first (“creeps up on us again”) and that they want and need to make their panic attacks cease, and are probably going to need help with that.

English translation: “One, two, three, four, five”.

Counting is a common coping skill for panic attacks, since focusing on slowly counting is a good way to center yourself and slow down your breathing. Alternatively, the counting could represent the progression of the panic attack, or the many panic attacks the speaker is having.

This lyric translates to “One, two, three, four, five / I will not go on a walk with you”.

Counting is a common coping skill for panic attacks, since focusing on slowly counting is a good way to center yourself and slow down your breathing. Alternatively, the counting could represent the progression of the panic attack, or the many panic attacks the speaker is having.

“I will not go on a walk with you” – This could be saying that “you” is causing the speaker extra stress, so they don’t want to be with them and break down until they are in control again. More likely, it is saying that the speaker is in no state to go hang out.

Just like the others verses, Tolokonnikova talks about her mental health, but in these lines, she explains how she is dealing with that: taking pills.

In the music video description, she commented that she struggles with mental issues, feeling insecure, having depression episodes, and deep anxiety after serving two years in a labor camp.

According to Tolokonnikova, in the music video description, depression is a plague of the 21st century and describes how we mistreat each other. As KFF stated, in the COVID-19 pandemic, about 4 in 10 adults in the USA have reported symptoms of anxiety. In 2020, more than 40% of the adult population in the USA reported having depression and/or anxiety.

An ashtray is a small recipient used for leaving tobacco and cigarette ends. The main vocalist, Nadezhda Tolokonnikova, alludes this object to her sentiments: she feels that everyone can use her, but because she is “so decayed”, she won’t do anything about it. According to Coin Telegraph, Nadezhda was feeling helpless at the music creation time.

metadata.title: Afraid
annotation: The last chorus changes perspective on who’s saying it. This time, Ryan tells the girl he’s afraid, while also telling her that she will hold onto this pain of letting him down.
The girl does these things to make Ryan feel alone because she’s afraid of letting him down. She’s afraid of feeling miserable once their relationship fails.

A play on the phrase, “There’s no place like home”, where your home is the place you feel most comfortable in. In this case, he doesn’t feel this way because the girl he’s with shuts him out and ignores him. He feels alone even though he’s with her.
He loves her but they fight so much he wonders why he keeps trying, especially when she leaves him.

metadata.title: One
annotation: The concluding line suggests that despite the challenges and manipulation, individuals possess an inherent awareness of the truth and interconnectedness. It implies that through unity and collective consciousness, people can overcome these obstacles.

These lines criticize the role of media and its influence on society. Cleo questions how society has allowed these issues to persist, referencing the consumption of false narratives and distractions perpetuated by media.
These lines highlight the current state of the world, expressing concern about environmental destruction and the emotional distress it causes. “How, how” emphasizes her disbelief at the situation.

These lines express a comforting presence, offering support to the listener. The imagery of holding hands and letting go suggests this, while the mention of an echo emphasizes a continuous connection between individuals.

These lines highlight the theme of unity and interconnectedness. Despite the feeling of being alone, Cleo reassures that it’s okay because we are ultimately connected and can find support in one another.

These lines emphasize the impermanence of material possessions, suggesting that everything could be lost, including one’s soul. It reflects on the fleeting nature of life and the need to prioritize what truly matters.
These lines question the notion of ownership and material possessions, implying that they are temporary and transient.
Cleo clarifies that the fight is not against herself, indicating a refusal to engage in self-destructive behavior or self-blame.

metadata.title: Afraid
annotation:
Although Jesse could be worried about other people having the same fears as he does, he’s more likely expressing a fear about not being authentic anymore.

These lines aren’t literally meant, they imply an unawareness for the changes to his personality, which cause him to become unauthentic. In that sense, to wake up means to realise this difference.

All day, Jesse walks around frightened to do anything. His only source of comfort is his relationship, but even that is one of his biggest causes for stress. Using sleep as an extended metaphor throughout the song, he asks his girlfriend to release him from her tormenting grasp, and give him a peaceful rest and wake up.

Even when he’s sleeping, he’s vulnerable to showing his weaknesses and insecurities, but wants his friends to ignore their findings. Now, he’s lacking in a faith in anything, a point addressed on the first song on the album, “How”.

Even with the turmoil that goes on in the relationship, Jesse advises himself to keep on with his life, and not to completely detach himself, only suggesting to sell his soul, and not his body and mind.
While his friends are telling him that his relationship is fine, Jesse knows that internally, they’re actually thinking that it’s on the rocks and on the way out soon.
Even though she’s putting on a happy face, Jesse can tell that internally, she’s about to begin making things hard on him again.

After his girlfriend pesters him to the point of feeling sick, Jesse understands that she’s constantly going back-and-forth with being satisfied.

He is constantly going up and down with his  feelings about his career, relationship, and future. He’s plagued with the thought that he could lose his life and livelihood to “the next big thing”.

He seems to be talking about himself (and maybe creating an insight into the future of his career) throughout the entire song. If you watch the music video, there is no girl at any instance. Near the end, the blinking eye that has served as a frame up until this point zooms out and reveals to be his own eye. Jesse has been watching everything that was happening, because he just woke up, and he saw himself. This song is not about a romantic relationship as many people have interpreted it to be — it is about Jesse’s future. But ultimately this song can be understood in many contexts, this just seems like the intended one.
This message of insecurity opens up the song, setting the tone for the lyrics to follow. The spacey feel of the intro makes it seem as if he’s just woken up, with this fear possibly being realized.

metadata.title: ​overwhelmed
annotation:
The intro of this song features the sound of a TV playing, channels switching through speeches and advertisements.

The “suspicious activity” could be an allusion to two things: a possible murderer or the supernatural. Both often cause anxiety, with other-worldly powers and a person bent on killing both unsavory prospects.



The poster used in the 1984 film Ghostbusters to attract costumers to a paranormal-terminator business




“The virus” is an allusion to the coronavirus pandemic. Beginning in December 2019, though truly making its mark in March of 2020, the coronavirus pandemic (or COVID-19) caused people to have to quarantine in their homes. The pandemic was an international cause of panic, inspiring anxiety in many who were vulnerable to the virus, thus its cameo in a song that speaks of anxiety attacks.
The singer feels as if someone’s mind is in hers, making her do things that she wouldn’t have done outside of her anxiety. And if someone else is doing stuff, why should the singer care.

Possible this could relate to the constant hyper-vigilance a person experiences when chronically anxious. This also could relate to a panic attack’s triggers, which often include large amounts of noise, crowds, and a lack of space to move.

When a person goes through the experience of an anxiety attack, or prolonged periods of anxiousness and/or depression dissociation can occur. Dissociation makes a person feel separate from their body, as if they are somebody else, like a trance has come over them and they no longer are in control.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: Dissociation can also make people feel as if they are separate from their environment, and removed from their experiences. It also causes people to feel less emotions.

The bridge of the song could be seen as a verse, but works like a bridge. This is the shortest part of the song besides the pre-chorus, showing the anxiety taking over the singer, making her almost unable to speak. The bridge is a summary of the verses and chorus in 2 sentences.
When some people feel anxious or have a panic attack, it can feel difficult or even impossible to speak
a person suffering from anxiety / panic attacks tends to escape from situations, even simple ones by isolating themselves from the things people say or do

Some people with anxiety can hate having people (usually people they don’t know) get close to them, try to hug them, etc. It makes them claustraphobic and makes them feel like they cant breathe. (NOTE: Not everyone with anxiety has this, and if you don’t have anxiety doesn’t mean you can’t feel this way.)

These lines point to an anxiety attack as it is common to have shortness of breath or not be able to breathe properly during one. During an anxiety/panic attack, breathing may become more shallow and/or restricted.

The person watching the TV is starting to get frightened from how loud the TV is. This could be because of over stimulation or a panic attack of some sort. It is common especially in children for feeling everything is too loud for them due to over stimulation.

metadata.title: My Idea of Fun
annotation:
Many children end up becoming emotionally mature at a really early age because of neglectful parents or loneliness and a lack of socialization

In adulthood, Pat feels lost and clueless as he knows many people (in contrast to him not knowing many kids) and sees them easily navigating through life

Not relying on the market for resources, in this case Pat suggests being self-sufficient is the way to go. Growing your own food as to not having to contribute to a capitalist society that produces conflict over limited resources.

Pat, being an activist, frequently has to field questions about the ideologies he portrays in his music. He appreciates the people who want to know more, but constantly talking about such emotionally draining concepts becomes very exhausting and he just wants to get away from it and talk about something else sometimes.

The Clash were one of the most important and influential acts in the history of punk rock. Their 1979 release London Calling is one of the most critically acclaimed album not just in the history of punk, but in rock in general.

But here, Pat disregards that. You don’t need a million-selling record to be a punk – we’re here, with the ideology and the attitude, and that’s enough.

Self-governing is the core of the ideology Pat expresses in much of his music, and that’s seen here and throughout the rest of the song. He doesn’t just want to abolish the police for the sake of it; he imagines a society – or, at least, a neighborhood – where people can take care of themselves and help one another, eliminating the need for official “help” in the form of a police force.
Pat makes the correlation that when his friend wants to die she shoots heroin, he also implies that she’s been found by the law “shooting dope” on numerous occasions

Pat is talking about how the law treats junkies, and makes it clear that arresting a junkie is essentially the same as arresting someone for being suicidal, In addition he refers to his neighbor in St Petersburg (Florida), who was arrested and ultimately put on house arrest for being a junkie.

“Work at home archaeologists, they dig skin deep, they work hard every day, On burying their arms for a vein or two that maybe they forgot” Means his friends became addicts, who shoot up everyday. This drug use is also referenced in the end of the song
Marshall amps/speakers for music. Higher quality/Big Brand.
Here pat is implying that being homeless and unemployed, requires just as much effort (if not more) than a typical workaday full time job

Many artists move to Brooklyn, a thriving borough in New York which has a reputation for fostering creativity. However, the cost of living is very high, due in part to gentrification. Patrick rejects the idea that artists must move to a new, expensive, “fancy” town to be considered real artists. He claims that a real artist can make art wherever they are, and that his current location is enough to foster his own creativity.

Here, Patrick mentions his desire for the anarcho-communist utopia, which is the subject of many of his songs. In Jesus Does The Dishes, he references this building of a new world as The Revolution, which is a reference to Karl Marx’s theory of a working class revolt.

Pat often refers to jail as a cage. For instance in, Urine Speaks Louder than words, he sings:

Pay no attention while millions get locked in a cage.

This speaks to his anarchist belief that the government treats us like animals and we would be better off without them.
In communism the is never going to be a boss. Pat is talking about abolishing this in favor of something else. Perhaps workers councils wich favor direct democracy within a workplace.

The line is “Even the suburbs know power’s getting too crooked to stand on it’s own feet for much longer than it has.” The suburbs are generally places where complacency is fairly entrenched, so “even the suburbs” knowing that systems of power in existence are corrupt would be a sign that systems of power in existence are Very corrupt.

metadata.title: Faith
annotation:
The faith that Calvin seeks may seem cursorily obvious, but it is actually very unclear what he means.

A glance at Motion’s tracklist reveals that the overarching theme of self-doubt in a relationship pervades the first 15-20 minutes of the album, with the tracks “Under Control”, “Blame” and “Love Now” all describing Calvin and his lover under some stress. Perhaps then, the faith he seeks is from his lover, for her to bestow “hope” and “strength”, or perhaps it is a cry to himself, to have a little more faith that he can get through this.



Or perhaps, with Faith’s position as the opening track, Calvin might want listeners to have faith in what he is about to deliver. Expectations are high, especially given his explosive release, “18 Months”, 2 years ago. He might be requesting listeners to have faith in the formula which has worked wonders thusfar. He might even be pleading to fans who liked his work before his shift in tone from nu-House to Electro-House to give him a second chance with Motion. With the release of Funk Wav Bounces Vol. 1, we might even retrospectively conclude that Calvin’s plea might be to have faith in the stylistic changes to come, although that might be a stretch.



Perhaps Calvin might have wanted us to have a little faith in everything, who knows?

metadata.title: Lost in a Wave
annotation: Possibly a metaphor for a panic attack
Possibly a metaphor for a panic attack
Euphemism for suicide

This verse could be describing a panic attack, having a panic attack increases the chance of having another hence “It’s a feeling I know” and symptoms of panic attacks include:
- heightened senses or sensory overload “all my senses are heightened”

-temporary paralysis (due to overwhelming anxiety) “I can’t move at all”

Feeling waves crashing down could be a metaphor
for anxiety, and “these words are useless” could be
describing an attempt to calm someone having a
panic attack down, but often people experiencing
a panic attack may not even notice the person
   speaking.

https://www.nhs.uk/mental-health/feelings-symptoms-behaviours/feelings-and-symptoms/anxiety-fear-panic/

metadata.title: Cancer / Moonspeak
annotation: Those who the narrator feels pressure from, possibly no more than fictional manifestations of his own guilt, see him in all his insufficiency, all his shortcomings and failures. Their judgment, or maybe more precisely the judgement of his own conscience, is “real”, maybe more real than anything else (his suffering).
The narrator’s conscious experience is consumed by fear, and by extension his world is in chaos (consumed by fear); everything is interesting.

metadata.title: Trapped in the Closet Chapter 3
annotation: Gay marriage is against the religion of Christianity, so this is definitely pretty crazy for a Christian pastor to say.

During the previous cliffhanger, we find out that the “lady” the husband sweet talked over the phone is actually a man, indicating the husband is homosexual and was seeing men on the side while he was married.

Kells and the woman are in total shock at this twist, which is understandable, because of how angry the husband seemed after finding of his wife’s infidelity, and….oh right, HE’S MARRIED.
Rip my boy on the sixth floor

One of the fun meta points about Trapped, “three” is an unusually specific number of minutes (usually one, five, or ten would be used) to allow Chuck time to explain. Instead, three minutes is approximately the time of standard pop songs, the format of which this series builds upon.

So these people are wrong for cheating, now he is going to presumably return to his wife/girlfriend and things will be fine

“You shouldn’t throw stones if you live in a glass house”
It’s not that surprising that a woman would use a fake name when she’s cheating on her husband, but this is Trapped in the Closet
So the thrust of Rufus’s argument is that the fact that his wife was cheating in their home and got caught it is much worse than his creeping outside of the home
These type of vocal acrobatics are what make the Trapped in the Closet series so fun and really showcase R. Kelly’s talent

text: I’m sick of being ignored
output:
1) **Looking Over My Shoulder** - **Elliott Smith**
   This song captures the feeling of being overlooked and ignored, with lyrics like "Another sick rock 'n' roller acting like a dick". It's a melancholic folk tune that perfectly resonates with your current emotion.

2) **Waiting for a War** - **The Morning Benders**
   This song expresses feelings of frustration and impatience, as shown in the lyrics "I had enough, either give me what I want or put me on the streets". The upbeat tempo and slightly acoustic sound add to its relatable appeal.

3) **Common People** - **Street Dogs**
   This punk song talks about disillusionment with social norms and the feeling of being sick of it, as expressed in the lyrics "I'm tired of American socialite culture". It's a high-energy track that might help you vent your feelings.

4) **Everybody Knows My Name** - **Harley Poe**
   This punk song speaks about feeling ignored and unnoticed, as shown in the lyrics "I'm the one, I am ignored". The raw energy and emotion in this track make it a powerful choice for your current mood.

5) **Telephone** - **Flipper**
   This punk song expresses feelings of loneliness and longing, as shown in the lyrics "Now when i'm sick and tired and i'm far away from home I need to hear your voice on the telephone". It might provide some comfort during times of feeling overlooked.

metadata.title: No One Noticed
annotation: This  line again highlights the songs theme of Maria feeling this way for some time (see “its getting old”)
This line shows the fleeting nature of the singers presence in the other’s life

In an interview with Genius Verified, María explained:

This is the part of the song where that virtual connection tries to make itself tangible. It’s this desperation of like, ‘Don’t leave me, I will see you in person, I want to see you in person. I will get on a flight in the middle of the night, show up at your doorstep in the morning, do a grand gesture to show you just how much this means to me.’ I’m a person of grand gestures. I love romance and I love to be romanced and I love romancing. I’m like Noah in ‘The Notebook’, I’m not like Ally, I’m like Noah, like, I will build you a house. I don’t know how to build a shelf from IKEA, but I will learn how to build you a house if I love you enough. And so it’s that gesture of like, ‘I’m just gonna fly to you, and show you how much you mean to me.’”

In an interview with Genius Verified, María explained:

At the beginning of the song it’s like no one is noticing, like, I feel alone. Here’s where the song is saying, ‘Oh wow, like, I feel seen now,’ like this warm feeling of ‘somebody understands me,’ but knowing that, ‘Wait a minute, like, this might not be right.’ So that’s where the back and forth starts.

In an interview with Genius Verified, María explained:

It represents that it (your mental struggles) has been going on for quite some time and that I’m just tired of this feeling. Like, ‘I wish that you could understand what I’m going through.’ Even if I explain it and scream what’s going on, it’s not getting through. It’s kind of that breakdown of, I guess, communication of not being able to understand each other.

These lyrics convey the feeling of loneliness and invisibility, when someone is struggling inside without others even noticing. María acknowledges that while it’s not anyone’s responsibility to read a person’s mind, small acts of awareness can make a difference. Simple gestures, like noticing nervous habits (for example, biting one’s nails) can help someone feel seen. She expanded on this herself during an interview with Genius Verified:

It’s just kinda playing on, you know you could be in a room full of people, or in a room with somebody that has no idea what’s going on inside of you. And you know, you could be just going through the darkest period of your life and nobody, nobody would know and nobody would even try to notice or try to ask you about it, so I think at the time, I was just feeling kind of a little bit invisible. Even though I understand it’s nobody’s responsibility to read your mind, I feel like it’s your responsibility to communicate how you’re feeling, but at the same time, it’s kind of nice when people pick up on little things. ‘Looks like you’ve been biting your nails, are you nervous about something?’ I feel like you can tell a lot about my state of mind based on how my nails are that day. Little things like that when you can pick up on that. Or when they think you’re cold and give you a blanket, things like that that make you feel seen, or noticed.

This line is ambiguous – she could be saying that it shouldn’t be so easy for her partner to leave, or it could be interpreted as self-critical; saying that ‘it can’t be that easy’ to stay with her, as if it takes effort, or she views herself as a burden.

The ambiguity could present an inner conflict/cognitive dissonance of sorts – she is unsure whether to blame her partner or herself.

Extended outro played at npr’s tiny desk:
I wanted to stay
Wanted to be there
Wanted to hold you
But I, I was afraid
Wanted to be there
I should’ve told you

Starting at the second iteration of the chorus, an echo of Maria’s voice begins to be heard, shown in parentheses on this page. This is a similar style to a canon in Anglican chant, where one voice part begins singing a verse, and the rest of the parts join in eventually, creating a beautiful melody that is both indescribable and incomprehensible.

Using this element of the composition, the Marias enforce the whole song’s ideas of confusion, loneliness, and heartbreak by giving voice to the usually-silent choir within Maria’s own head.

A gentle & hopeful wish to slow down and savour each moment together if she had the chance. Wanting to move the relationship with care and allowing it to grow in its own pace. The sense of wanting to be deliberate and present, letting everything unfold naturally and not forcing an outcome.

Negotiating the luxury of time together.

The beginning and hesitant thought that’s full of possibilities and negotiation. The swirling inner dialogue of wanting something but not being sure if it’s the right thing or if it even matters anymore.

Such as; ‘maybe I could have done more’, ‘maybe I could still make things right’, ‘maybe I should move on’, ‘maybe I shouldn’t have let go’, etc.

The open ended feeling of wondering ‘what if’, second guessing your choices. Being caught between wanting to act and being afraid of the outcome. The fragile space where you question everything – yourself, your emotions, and whether trying again would make a difference. The endless weighing of options and possibilities but never finding the clear answer.

Her willingness to chase being close to him, no matter the cost and length. Even if it is brief, the thought of seeing him again would make it feel real for a second. This love is making her feel impulsive and fuelled by emotion. With the hope that that seeing him in-person  will change things.
The repeated lines, “I’d kinda like it if you’d call me” and “I need a virtual connection,” reveal a deep desire for interaction and emotional support.

A video obsession is clearly in reference to a person who only communes using electronic means, serving as a anaphoric reference to the use of ‘FaceTime’ in track 5, ”Real Life”

But it also serves to accentuate the distance between her and her partner, relating to him as a video obsession and a virtual connection, and not anything in the physical landscape; a concept in which is explored many times throughout the albums narrative, even being depicted specifically through the album art, with María deeply submerged, a far distance from the surface

text: I just left my girlfriend at the airport, and I am not going to see her for 3 months
output:
1) **Light Bulb Blues** - **The Shadows of Knight**
   This song perfectly captures the feeling of heartache and longing after a breakup. The lyrics about losing a woman and not knowing where you are at resonate with your situation.

2) **Gotta Get the First Plane Home** - **The Kinks**
   This track is about missing someone dearly and wanting to return home as soon as possible, which seems fitting for your current state of mind. The upbeat tempo also suggests a sense of urgency that might help you cope with your emotions.

3) **I’m Coming Home** - **Elvis Presley**
   This song's title and lyrics about the hardship of leaving someone you love will surely strike a chord with you. The emotional tone and slow tempo make it an ideal choice for expressing feelings of sadness and longing.

4) **Going Someplace to Forget** - **David Ball**
   This song's title implies escaping from current troubles, which seems relevant to your situation of wanting to forget about the distance between you and your girlfriend. The lyrics also suggest a desire to leave town, similar to your plans for travel.

5) **Other side of hope** - **The Kings Of Nuthin’**
   This song's title suggests a journey towards hope, which could symbolize your anticipation for the reunion with your girlfriend. The lyrics about missing someone and waiting for their return also reflect your current feelings.

text: The coffee’s gone cold again

1) **It Just Ain’t Hit Me Yet** - **Eddie Rabbitt**
   This song captures the feeling of a cold, stale situation with its lyrics about a cold cup of coffee and a stale cigarette. The melancholic tone and country genre further emphasize this sentiment.

2) **Black Coffee** - **Julie London**
   This jazz classic beautifully portrays a sense of loneliness and longing, as expressed in the lyrics "I'm feelin' mighty lonesome, haven't slept a wink." The title itself also references the coldness of the situation.

3) **Numbness for Sound** - **Howie Day**
   This indie song has a slow tempo and melancholic tone that matches your request. The lyrics "A cold Winter sun / My feet underground" further emphasize the feeling of being stuck in a cold, lonely place.

4) **One Rung** - **Slobberbone**
   This country song's lyrics about waking up to a closing-in world and feeling trapped ("Now, it's three a.m And the walls are closin' in") resonate with the idea of a cold situation that hasn't changed.

5) **Forty Cups Of Coffee** - **Ella Mae Morse**
   This jazz song's title and lyrics about drinking coffee to cope with loneliness ("Pace the floor, stop and stare / I drink a cup of coffee and start pulling out my hair") make it a fitting choice for your request.

metadata.title: Here Comes That Rainbow Again
annotation:
Kris Kristofferson was inspired by a scene from a movie based off of Steinbeck’s novel, The Grapes of Wrath.

The scene Kristofferson is painting here is nearly directly from the movie. In the movie (set during the Great Depression), a poor man came into a roadside café and asked to buy a loaf of bread for a poor woman with no teeth. After working out a deal with the owner, the man asks for two penny candies for his two children. The lady behind the register lies and told him that the candies were two for a penny, just like in Kristofferson’s song.

Here is the timestamped scene from the movie.

metadata.title: Roses
annotation: The main character doesn’t remember the pictures he took last night, probably because he got stupidly drunk; to the point of blacking out.

The singer drunk called his ex and said some things he regrets.

Because of this, he wishes her phone was dead; that way he would never have said all those embarrassing things to her last night.

The singer no longer sleeps in the same room as he does when he was with his ex, who he is singing to in these lines.
He likely moved to a spare bedroom, or slept on the couch to avoid the pain of the memories through smell, because the bed sheets still have his ex’s perfume on them.

He hasn’t washed the bed sheets because it hurts too much to let go of the memories. Because of this, when he sleeps in his old room, he wakes up smelling like the bed sheets, which smell like his ex’s perfume
This line refers to a story from the bassist who was invited out by a friend who claimed that Jay-Z was at the place they were inviting him out to.

The official Roses music video features an extended ending in which they sing
“Don’t let them grow too much
‘Cause thorns will proceed to touch
And your nerves are to blame
Wake up alone insane
So roses proceed to bloom
So I’ll rearrange my room
Cut off all of my hair
SOS in Bel-Air”

The singer, seeing as he was on a night out, possibly met some people to hang out with during the remainder of the night, and even got some pictures with them. After enough alcohol, though, comes a blackout, and with a blackout comes a hangover, leading to turmoil such as the one described here.

The VIP, a place where only the “elite” people can be, is guarded by an ex-marine.
…wow that actually kind of rhymed.
Anyways, the singer tried crashing the VIP  and… well… yeah.

“Last night I thought I met Jay-Z” is in reference to when bass player James' friend was invited out to a party that Jay-Z was supposedly at.

“Woke up still soaked in your perfume” may tell that the singer went to his girlfriend’s house after the night out and they slept in the same bed, and, as a result, he woke up with her perfume smell.
Main character of the song doesn’t want to be reminded of his girlfriend
The main character of the song gave his girlfriend roses because he thought she liked roses when she didn’t

metadata.title: Weekend
annotation:
Should be “Imma sleep in”
The song is all about treating weekdays like the weekend and what do you do on the weekends? Sleep in

“Weekend” was co-written by lil aaron, whose most famous track on which he appears as an artist is the Y2K collaboration “Damn.” Though Icona Pop says this word differently than in the hook of the latter song, he’s found great success with the word.
cf. ILoveMakonnen’s “Tuesday” for the most famous contemporary example of enjoying oneself on days usually dedicated to working.

There are various ways to be your own enemy and there are so many different consequences of missing self respect. In this regard they party too hard, drank too much and lost their memories. However they notice but can’t stop treating weekdays like the weekend.

text: The sky has been gray for days and it's never going to clear
output:
1) **Melancholia (Bonus)** - **40 winks**
   This song perfectly captures the feeling of a gray sky that never clears. The lyrics repeat "There's no sun in the sky," which directly addresses your mood, and the low valence suggests a somber tone.

2) **Stormy Weather** - **Dinah Washington**
   This jazz classic expresses feelings of sadness and longing, much like your current state. The lyrics mention "stormy weather" and "no sun up in the sky," making it a fitting choice.

3) **Eclipse** - **John Denver**
   John Denver's "Eclipse" is about the slow fading of the sun in the western sky, which resonates with your sentiment of a gray sky that never clears. The acoustic instrumentation adds to the melancholic feel.

4) **Since You Said Goodbye** - **J.J. Cale**
   This song's lyrics mention "rain keeps fallin' on my head" and "sun keeps burnin' out my eyes," reflecting your feelings of gloominess. The low energy and valence also contribute to the somber atmosphere.

5) **Sun & Moon** - **Above & Beyond**
   Although this song has a danceable beat, its lyrics describe a "black sky is falling" and "cold tonight," which aligns with your mood. The melancholic tone of the lyrics contrasts with the upbeat tempo, creating an interesting juxtaposition.

metadata.title: Shadow
annotation: Optimists and pessimists are inherently opposites. His negativity can not prevail when there is so much positivity in the world soiling it. It is his duty to destroy this happiness so that his pessimistic ideals can be pushed forward.

The lyricist plans to wage a war against the world’s optimists. There are people in this world who see the good, who believe the world is good. The lyricist has made it his business to convert these people into the philosophy that he holds: that the world is evil.

He states that it is in his hands, as if it is a godsend that he convert these people. That it is his responsibility to “fix” the minds of these mistaken optimists.

This line is about how dark the world is and how the lyricist wishes there be more light.

“Sun” is a metaphor for goodness; for the positivity in the world.

Stating its absence is saying there is nothing good in the world.

Asking it to glow is sarcasm. The lyricist knows there is nothing good in the world and is here joking about that fact.

metadata.title: Sun & Moon
annotation: When time begins to move forward, and the singer and the girl are trying to move on, only the good memories start to bubble up again.
http://images.rapgenius.com/4a350f73761f16e13cea345904dfd7d8.900x602x1.jpg
He loves his girl and his girl loves him, no matter what. Even if they are not together, they will never get over each other.
When he was with his girl, he was in heaven, all was perfect. He felt as if when he was with her, anything was possible, and nothing was impossible.

You really never know the odds to anything in life, it’s just chance. If you don’t try, you’ll never succeed, you have to try. Even though things probably won’t work out, you never know if you don’t try.
Much like gambling, there are odds to gambling and your odds are low, but if you never play, you’ll never win.
After she leaves him, he’s alone.
His girl gave him the answer, she no longer want to be with him, he’s left heartbroken.
An analogy that she was his everything. Like the Sun rotates the earth during the day and the Moon at night, she was always with him in his heart and there for meant the world to him.
The dark sky is falling and it’s raining because the relationship between the singer and his lover is falling apart

text: I made a lot of mistakes I don’t know how to forgive myself
output:
1) **Unforgiven** - **Rotting Out**
   This song speaks directly to feelings of guilt and self-loathing, with lyrics that echo your sentiment about making mistakes. The raw, emotional punk genre adds intensity to the track, helping you express your inner turmoil.

2) **Past The Past** - **New Medicine**
   In this rock song, the artist acknowledges the burden of past mistakes and the struggle to move forward. Lyrics such as "So now I've got baggage And don't I know I bear that cross" resonate with your current emotional state.

3) **Suffer in Silence** - **Apoptygma Berzerk**
   This electronic track addresses the theme of regret and the desire to forget past mistakes. The lyrics, "I need to forget And make this tragic feel better," reflect your wish for self-forgiveness.

4) **The Power Process** - **Incendiary**
   This punk song discusses forgiveness as a virtue yet to be achieved and the raw pain that comes with it. Lyrics like "Forgiveness is a virtue that I've yet to achieve" echo your feelings of not being able to forgive yourself.

5) **Fresh Out of Forgiveness** - **Dolly Parton**
   In this country ballad, the artist expresses a reluctance to forgive someone who has caused pain. The lyrics, "Don't tell me you're sorry for pain you caused me," may help you find solace in knowing that it's okay to hold onto your feelings of hurt and anger.

metadata.title: Danielson
annotation: I believe the narrator is realizing that all of his friends can’t stay in the city forever either. He could also be talking directly to his love interest in the last two lines. He’s sad that things have changed but he’s starting to grow up and realize that getting away from him and the city has made her a better person.
The narrator feels it may be easier to just forgot about a relationship with his love Interest and asks her to simply write to him instead. He pushes her away.
His love interest has invited him somewhere with her and her friends and he’s nervous about what they’ll think of him and if he will really have fun like she said.

Again, possibly referring to that summer after senior year, the narrator says it’s not for everyone. For some it’s very bittersweet or maybe just bitter because they know they are leaving something behind or someone is leaving them behind. The narrator probably feels he’s being left behind my his love interest but she swears that this summer is fun for him and that it’s more sweet than it is bitter. He’s not convinced
The narrator may feel stupid for asking his love interest to come see him before she goes off to wherever she may be going. He decides to just leave

This may be biased because I discovered this song my senior year of high school, right before I was about to leave many of my friends and my girlfriend behind to join the military.
But I believe the narrator is referring to a place, he calls the city, that he had to just enjoy his friends company while it’s still there.
However, in the last two lines he seems to be talking to someone who’s more than a friend. Someone who doesn’t want to join in on this “magical” place (the city) he and all his friends hang out at. He understands her desire to leave the city and move on to better things but does hope she comes to see him once before she leaves.

metadata.title: Summer Time High Time
annotation: The girl heard the song, she didn’t care. At the time, I wasn’t doing shit, so she didn’t really care. At the time, I was stoked for it. I was like, “yo this tight”. I don’t know what she thought about it, hopefully she liked it.

I’m talking about the gas prices. Just how they goin up. Economy and shit. I had a girlfriend at the time, and we were going to a fair, and she was pumping gas, and I was writing the lyrics. So I was like whatever, I’m just put the pump in there, she’s pumping gas. It wasn’t nothing deep.

I wrote this shit when I was 16. So, I don’t know what the fuck I was talking about. I know that I have gotten drunk in the back of a trunk once. Like a pickup truck, it was tight. So that’s why I was like hey we could get drunk in the back of a trunk. I’ve did it before, it’s pretty cool.

I feel like going to outer space is just getting the fuck away from everything dude. Sometimes, its not even just about being with somebody. Sometimes you just wanna get the fuck away from shit, dude. Like, sometimes bro, I love my city, and I love everything, I love Cali. But sometimes, fuck that shit dude. I just wanna get the fuck away from everything. I’m saying I wanna find somebody with the same mentality, that’s just like, “fuck doing the same shit everyday, fuck routines, fuck everything”. Open yourself up, understand there’s so much shit to do out there bro. I literally hate, sometimes just staying in one fucking place. Cause the fuckin sky’s the limit. It’s not the limit. Fuck the sky the being the limit dude. The universe is infinite. Your limits are infinite.

That just flowed well I thought. I feel people say they’re on cloud 9, so I guess I think about levels. Cloud 9, cloud 30. It just a stupid thing. I thought it was funny in my head. Then the corny ass line, it’s like “my highest is with you”.

I feel like the summer of 2016 was pretty tight. I actually wasn’t even talking to anybody, I was single as fuck. I think happiness is back, kinda pointed out my music going off. There was a time where I was just writing a bunch of love songs. That’s my discography for the most part. So “happiness is back, ain’t no one to me but you.” I guess it is kinda a reference, to psychedelics. I think whenever I would trip, I’m not talking about microdose, like actual heavy ass dose. I was trippin balls, I felt very at ease with myself, very bliss.

That’s a combination of my imagination, and different ideas, and influences I had. I was listening to Louie Armstrong, “Blueberry Hill.” That song is like, “I found my thrill, on blueberry hill”. I just imagined that, being on a hill. Obviously on a pretty pill, some shit that got you high as fuck. So that line is kind of influenced by Louie Armstrong, and off the Gorillaz. That was the inspiration behind it.

Summers in Cali are really dope. They get really hot. I think, after touring, I found out Cali has it really tight. Everywhere else is humid as fuck. Has terrible weather, in Cali even if it gets hot, you can still get away with wearing a long sleeve, or a sweater. Just being able to go around cruise, skate, kicking it with your homies. If you’re with somebody, kicking it with them is always tight. I think for me, driving to the beach, is tight. Just dead ass just chillin by the ocean. It’s cool, cause I live probably 10, 15 minutes from Manhattan, Rodondo. I don’t have plans on what my summers are. I dead ass just be kicking it. Just be chillin.

Coming up with the melody wasn’t that hard. I’m always just doing leads, then my voice always just follows the leads. Hearing the first words that came to my mouth were “summer time.” It’s obviously a love song. That’s obviously, what a lot of my vibe is. It just kinda came together as a hook.

metadata.title: Smoke Ya Later
annotation: This is a reference to intercourse where the male uses the eye socket as the point of penetration and is known colloquially as “skull fucking”.
The killer is remorseless; he has heard people say that to him before. He wants her on her knees begging for forgiveness and expressing her devotion to him.
He compares the sky and the grass which are now both a shade of red. As the victim bleeds from her eye sockets she apologizes, that she had wronged him somehow.

He has a strange infatuation with this victim which is very common for a serial killer. His Modus Operandi may be to gouge out the eyes of his victims. His reason for this could be a pathological rage that is centered around the ability of sight.

It’s almost as if he’s telling her “If you’re too ashamed or too afraid to look at me I’ll punish you in a way so you can’t see at all.”
The sky is red which would seem to denote a sunset. He likens it to the blood that poured from the eye sockets of a victim when he gouged out her eyes.
With the helicopters gone he can finally see what’s above him. His chase may have been long before he sky or escaped incarceration and there was no view of the sky in his cell.
Vincent describes being pursued heavily by the police, in this case by helicopter. The structure of the song lends these lines to be more of a preface the description of events that follow.

metadata.title: C’est La Vie
annotation:
These three lines present a gradual change in the emotional state of the singer after her breakup. While at first Tinashe calmly acknowledges the idea that letting go off people is an inevitable but crucial part of our life, later on, the lyrics imply that she might not be that certain about whether the decision to let go off her lover was the right one. The first line fits the nonchalant/untroubled mood set by the opening lines of the verse as she is about to light up a blunt and not care about anything and anyone. The image of her taking a flight also implies the extent to which she is over the breakup – she is ready to leave everything behind and begin her life from a clean slate anywhere else.



 However, the next line switches up the mood as she starts contemplating about staying for longer, as if not entirely sure whether she wants to leave her former partner. As she leaves, she starts regretting the breakup and begs her lover to come back and stay with her.

VVS stands for Vertical Video Syndrome.  People who shoot videos vertically are believed to have VVS.  Tinashe be shooting her videos from head to toe as she wants her whole frame captured because she looks good, from head to toe.

  

A photo posted by TINASHE (@tinashenow) on Sep 20, 2016 at 12:33pm PDT



 

VVS is also a certain diamond category – Very, Very Slightly Included category (VVS) diamonds have minute inclusions that are difficult for a skilled grader to see under 10x magnification. The VVS category is divided into two grades; VVS1 denotes a higher clarity grade than VVS2. She could also therefore, be saying that she stays covered up in diamonds from head to toe.

metadata.title: Goodness Pt. 2
annotation:
Maintaining the same theme as the previous lines, only when joy and sorrow coexist may we begin to live our lives and share our experiences with those around us.

Note that the coexistence of goodness and depression is a major theme not only throughout this song, but the rest of the album.

In life we experience a multitude of different emotions, each directing us towards a different path that we may choose to follow. However, if we do not make rash decisions based on our varying emotions, we may calmly tune out these feelings until we are at peace.

Spinning without a compass symbolizes how our emotions affect us to go towards the unknown. In the end however, we’re simply spinning in place, winding up at the same place each time. Our feelings may tear us apart, however as we battle through it, we come to the same place we were before.

As Holden began to move on from the depression of the past to who he is now, the memories of what he used to be clings to his mind, trying to drag him back into the sadness. The thaw here represents this shift from the “colder” days to the warm, from Holden’s depression to a chance for happiness.

As Holden experiences this growth, nature calls out to him, helping him reach a calm state between joy and sadness, something Holden hopes he might be able to do for someone in a similar state.

It’s interesting to note the difference in the influence of the bird from it’s use on “An Introduction to the Album” on their previous release, Home Like Noplace Is There. This song states:

Singing bird tells me
“Tear the buildings down”

This change of mood from anger to calm represents Holden’s change in attitude during the time between these two albums.

When we as humans are stripped of all the commodities we’ve come accustomed to such as electronics and even clothes, we take our place in nature as it was in the beginning. Humans came billions of years after the earth was created: our timeline in the grand scheme in the world is an incredibly small fragment. This is not to say we find depression in feeling small; rather we’re ambivalent to the situation, finding hope in the comfort of what we’re used to. This constancy of humanity was discussed in an interview with The Fader in which Holden mentions how the lack of change allows for peace and calm.

metadata.title: Weightless
annotation:
On one level, this might be a reference to Mad Magazine’s Spy vs. Spy comics in which a white hat spy and and a black hat spy struggle to out-sneak each other.  Ludicrously, they might be so stealthy that they can hide behind each other’s back.

On a deeper level, it’s an elaboration about the way desires hide behind each other.

This line actually begins “Correct life”, not “Grown-up life” as it’s currently listed.  I think it refers to the Buddhist Eightfold Path describing right living (i.e. correct living): right view, right resolve, right speech, right conduct, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right meditation.

Trying to live according to these precepts is an intense experience.  It requires a relentless attention and commitment. It would be easier to go back to living in the dark.

This is a central part of Buddhist thought. Desire comes in a never ending chain. Satisfying desires does not lead to happiness because another desire will always arise.  True happiness comes from a calm awareness of how things actually are and an abandonment of self and desire.
“Climbing from over-stimulated states to hearing” is an apt description of what it can feel like when beginning a session of meditation.

I think this song is about Buddhist-style mindfulness meditation and how a meditative state relates to regular life, although this theme is certainly presented rather obliquely.

In Buddhist meditation, the concept of “the world as a dream” is a key teaching. Our perceived reality is impermanent, illusory, and ultimately not as solid as it seems, much like a dream, which can appear very real while we are experiencing it, but fades away upon waking up; this realization is meant to help practitioners detach from clinging to worldly experiences and move towards enlightenment.

Perceived reality is weightless.  Life outside of a mindful state is killing time. Things happen, but we are scarcely aware.

“No stairways, just stairs” might be a reference to Led Zeppelin’s Stairway to Heaven. The weightless affairs of regular outside life don’t form a stairway leading to heaven, they lead nowhere.  Enlightenment is found within.

metadata.title: Beloved
annotation:
These lines tell us that he is communicating with his beloved in a place where he is “with them” yet he can not reach them with his words, personally.  And he asks them, rhetorically, if they know the years have been passing, and will pass again, and that life is carrying on without them.

He continues that reminiscence is not the only reason he came to visit them. Rather, telling them his feelings about them, that he is seeking closure, even just imagining his beloved able to hear his words feels comforting to him.

The dead of winter casts a haunting silence, there are no leaves left for the wind to rustle, all the animals and people are tucked away somewhere warm.

He remarks that this quiet makes him focus on nothing but memories of his beloved and all the time he spent waiting for them to return to him.

The circumstances of the situation with his beloved gives him no second chance to tell them how much he has missed them, as they have passed away.

Ronan sets the scene for us. The season’s foliage bloomed in spring, flourished in the summer and the leaves have now fallen from the trees. It is winter, the ground now snow covered and “dressed in white and grey” the snowflakes seem to make winter “dance” upon their descent from the sky.

The reference to it being “fitting”  to “dress the ground in white and grey” is strikingly similar to the grey-scale observed in black and white classic movies from another era.

These lines make a strong metaphor to Ronan’s emotional state as he begins to reminiscing over someone ‘beloved’ he has lost that has passed away.

Here Ronan conveys the imagery of himself looking up at the clouds above him thinking of the time they spent together.  Sometimes thinking he can see them in the clouds above.  He imagines his beloved with him, watching over him.



These lines convey he is still grief-stricken by the loss.  Expressing to his beloved that losing them is a grief in which he feels will not easily pass over him, if it should pass at all.

Making reference to the previous lines in which he states the reason he came to visit his beloved, we now understand this reason more concisely as to communicate to his beloved that he still misses them, will never forget their time together, their accomplishments and is still thinking of, and mourning, losing them.

He remembers back to the time when they were young, free spirits.  Together, they were both an unstoppable force and they achieved great things.



They explored spirituality and grew in wisdom together, yet something burned within each of them. This pushed them further into the world to learn and explore.  As a result, this youthful companionship drifted apart.  Each of them following their own paths in life.

These lines are strikingly similar to the message conveyed in the famous poem by Robert Frost, The Road Not Taken

I shall be telling this with a sigh
Somewhere ages and ages hence:
Two roads diverged in a wood, and I—
I took the one less traveled by,
And that has made all the difference.

Ronan tells us through his conversation with his beloved that both of them took the “roads less traveled”.  Here, he reassures his beloved he doesn’t regret any choice that he’s made in life, and that he knows they feel the same way.

text: The walls feel like they are closing in
output:
1) **Steve French** - Flux Pavilion
    The intense energy and dark lyrics create a sense of confinement and pressure, mirroring your feelings. Lyrics like "Rising pressure feel the drop" emphasize this.

2) **Feeding Fear** - Crowbar
    This song's heavy, gloomy atmosphere and lyrics such as "Reaching for the surface I cannot feel it My lungs they feel like bursting" resonate with feelings of being trapped and overwhelmed.

3) **A Raindance in Traffic** - The Wonder Years
    Despite its upbeat tempo, the lyrics express a desire to escape and wash away one's troubles, which might help you cope with feeling closed-in. Lyrics like "I'm fantasizing about doing a raindance in traffic" illustrate this.

4) **She’s a Real Battleaxe** - Vanna
    The song's aggressive tone and lyrics such as "He waits while the city is sleeping, she takes her time" suggest a sense of tension and claustrophobia that aligns with your feelings.

5) **Nice Things** - The Menzingers
    Although it has a melancholic vibe, the song's lyrics like "The western wall is a jumbo screen At the gate, there is an automated teller machine" evoke feelings of being trapped or overwhelmed in a crowded space.
