metadata.title: A Raindance in Traffic
annotation:
This line may be referencing the stereotype in TV and movies where a character is caught in a major downpour, and it gives them an overwhelming sense of their mental and emotional problems being “washed away.”

However, here, this trope is turned on its head : Dan is so close to giving up he wishes the rain would wash him away, as if he were too beyond repair for redemption. He just wants to disappear — for a flash flood to sweep him away, never to be found again.
He feels disconnected and like he’s faking his personality constantly. He doesn’t feel like he can show his true emotions.

Continuing the WWII theme that is constant in The Greatest Generation is the idea that Dan’s trench is surrounded by the enemy. They have more fire-power than him and it is just a matter of time until they get to him.



This image symbolises Dan’s fight with mental illness. The world is throwing too many challenges at him, and he can’t keep up : he’s being buried underneath the sheer number of his assailants, and doesn’t have the coping strategies or the mental strength to fight back.

The windows literally being filled in with bricks symbolize that Soupy is trapped. The other idea is that he lives in very close proximity to other buildings and feelings surrounded by them.

Either way he is trapped.

The fighter Soupy is referring to is that of boxer as there are some http://www.imdb.com/title/tt0081398/ references in this song.



Soupy is watching his former self separate and become a ghost meaning his inner fighter is dead.
Soupy was young, vibrant, and chomping at the bit ready to take on the world. He felt so sure that he could handle anything thrown his way.

Another world-class line from Soupy.

Steady hands symbolise youth and confidence. Now after so many battles, Soupy is broken and his hands shake with uncertainty.

This is extremely similar to when the sure handed Wes Welker dropped the biggest play of his career. Dan is an avid football fan, and it would make sense for him to compare himself to a player fumbling an important ball.



His hands may also literally be shaking due to anxiety.

This line is a reference to the famous Martin Scorsese movie http://www.imdb.com/title/tt0081398/

“You dont understand. I coulda had class, I coulda been a contender, I coulda been somebody.”

http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KLNft6cO0I4

The monologue originated from this famous scene from On The Waterfront (1954)

https://youtu.be/uBiewQrpBBA

1929 was the year of the Wall Street Crash.
Soupy is either comparing his mind-frame to the 23,000 people who committed suicide in the ensuing year, or more likely to the collapse of the actual stock market itself, which left 12 million people unemployed.

Laugh-lines are wrinkles that appear around the mouth from the nose to the chin, along the creases of the “smile muscles” — hence the name. They are usually the first wrinkles to appear, as they are situated on an area that is often under stress.



Dan may seem like a happy and cheerful person at first glance, but all his laughing and smiling is only a façade : inside, he feels damaged and depressed, ready for a mental breakdown. If anything, his laugh lines are a red flag : he’s faking happiness, putting on a face to save his loved ones from worrying about his mental state — a common behaviour in people dealing with lifelong mental illness.

metadata.title: Nice Things
annotation:
Do you want ‘things’, do you want to feel safe?

Lonely and/or discontented people may seek comfort in the pursuit of materialism/accumulating belongings.

Perhaps also from the sales pitch perspective of a profit-motivated sales person/spruiker trying to sell products to a potential buyer and trying to play off the insecurities of scared/discontented people to make a sale

Dreams – American Dream?

“Singing songs of another time” They are nostalgic for a time when their nation/society was more prosperous and hopeful (Or perhaps just yearning for the days of peak-decadence, before economic collapse and poverty was quite so rampant).

Now ‘the Western walls are closing in’, prosperity and hope are fading

Nice things – materialism and status symbols?

“Do you call nice things your own?” could be interpreted as a question of wealth/social status

The question “Do you want nice things?” is answered immediately; Sure you do
But the question “Do you call nice things your own?” is left open.

Having the American Dream of consumerism and desire for wealth is assumed as true and guaranteed, while achieving it is not.

The king and queen ‘foreclosed’ on their crowns – which suggests that their ‘crowns’ (Probably a reference to status symbols such as luxury cars/ luxury homes etc) were brought with borrowed money, they were in debt to a lender and when they couldn’t keep up with repayments the lender foreclosed on them.
Possibly an analogy to the economic decline of the United States (and the effects of the GFC and foreclosure crisis – which financially ruined much of the indebted members of the middle/upper-middle class)

Possibly saying that in order to gain entry and achieve happiness you must first give up on everything you once had, financially, emotionally, and physically

Also could be a reference to immigrants who would give up everything they had to come to the United States through Ellis Island

Using Jerusalem’s Western Wall, the holiest site in Judaism, as a metaphor for the entirety of Western civilization, the singer decries it, and Western civilization along with it, as merely a massive television – the epitome of vapidness and transience.
This line is referencing fame. Do people know your name and wish to be you?
The West is collapsing economically . No one fears the WEstern powers anymore
Possibly the colonization of Africa and South America taking all of its gold
Telling the listener to escape before the walls ( mentioned in the first line of the 2nd verse) collapse around them. they need to escape before it is too late
A reference to the pursuit of happiness and what most ordinary people are looking to get out of their lives. it asks the question, “have you achieved the american dream”
About the collapse of the West as a “great” power

metadata.title: Drunk By Name
annotation: DJ Fuck, aka Sibot (real name Simon Ringrose) WTJ’s sidekick on the turntables who had a heavy affiliation with Waddy on his early work. The two would fall out during after this album. DJ Fuck under his Sibot alias Collaborated with WTJ (now in his Ninja guise in Die Antwoord) after 12 years by letting them use “corner” for the main beat of Peanutbutter + Jelly on the new Die Antwoord album “Mount Ninji and Da Nice Time Kid” in 2016.

Spoek Mathambo (born Nthato Mokgata 14 May 1985 in South Africa) is an artist, producer, singer-songwriter, rapper defined by his fusion of a wide array of musical influences and his coining the Township Tech, to describe the electronic music he produces.

Mathambo grew up in Soweto, South Africa.  To say his debut album came out in 2010, this is one of debut appearances he made in the south african music scene.  Waddy would later diss him in Die Antwoord due to his affiliation with ex collaborator Markus Wormstorm due to their partnership in Sweat X.
Miff is Afrikaans slang for something disgusting or gross.

The chorus of this track is basically a rewrite of the nursery rhyme “Teddy Bears Picnic” which dates back to 1907. Waddy injects his childish humor  over it, implementing how you should react to said track.
DJ Fuck uses a lot of video game samples in his music like MegaMan 2 (on the song Visitor) and Pacman (in the song Y-Front)

The name of Waddy’s daughter, who was born during the conception of this album. She can be heard crying as a baby as a hidden track after world champion on this album, and on the followup album as a toddler on Max Normal.Tv’s song “Moon Love.”

When Diz is chilling with his bros you can’t see him, he’s in private, but living in privacy while at home doesn’t mean he isn’t enjoying himself. He’s living it up, and people want to be him, but there’s only one Dizzee Rascal.
Dizzee is never lazy

Reference to 2Pac’s 4th studio album, which is often mentioned as his greatest album. Dizzee has also claimed Pac as an influence before and said “On my stereo, full blast, 2Pac” in his song Road Rage.
Whenever he releases a song, whether good or bad, he makes money. Dough is slang for money!

Dizzee’s in a fast car driving 160 miles per hour. While his claim that he takes less than 400 milliseconds to pass you by might be a bit of a stretch, the point is he’s going fast



This is pretty near the top speed in most cars

This ain’t a slow jam : Dizzee doesn’t want to fuck slowly, he’s ready to pick up the pace.

I’m gripping at the Trojan : Trojans are a brand of condoms. Dizzee already has the condom in his hand for the incoming hard sex.

The phrase: ‘If you can’t handle the heat, get out of the kitchen’ is used when somebody needs to remove them self from
a situation that is beyond their control.  Diz' point is that if he ever gets into this situation (either musically, or with respect to women), he will dip (leave) rather than stand there like a mug.

This could be a reference to the earlier line about Gripping a Trojan In terms of not getting any females pregnant during intercourse

Dizzee was misquoted by the media as having dissed his hometown of Bow in East London in an interview with UK newspaper The Sun about the Olympics Games and it’s impact on his hometown.



He said in context of the town’s degradation,

I don’t still live in Bow, but I go back all the time, and it’s s—. The whole area is just a big building hole.

Of course, he was in no way putting slack on Bow, he was talking about how the Olympics Games, whose Olympic Park was being built right next door, had turned Bow into such a “hole”.



This line is basically a reassurance that he is proud of his hometown, and will continue to represent it. E3 is simply the postcode of Bow and it’s surrounding suburbs,  Old Ford, Mile End and Three Mills, although most Londoners would refer to certain areas by their postcode, not their actual names.

No hipster shit over here, bruh.  Just gangsta shit.

Not everyone agrees with Drizzy:

And me doing them shows getting everyone nervous cause
Them hipsters going have to get along with them hood niggas
A chief executive officer (CEO) is the highest-ranking corporate officer (executive) or administrator in charge of total management of an organization.
A pun on the word “check”, referencing the chess term “Checkmate”.
He’s not giving the rap game his all. You don’t want to see what he’s like when he gets ‘abstract’ (creative) with his words.
Being mellow can mean simply being relaxed and chilled out, or being at a point of almost being high, but not quite there. Either way, Dizzee is is chilling out with his snapback cocked back.
Power Steering is a system in cars that helps the driver steer. He’s using this as a play on words for accuracy.
‘The sticks’ usually refers to a place almost in the middle of nowhere, or on the outskirts of town.

Dizzee uses this as a way to describe his wealth. He basically can go to all the great climates in the world and he doesn’t need a reason, because he is rich and when he wants more money he will just rap some more. This is very similar to former Manchester City forward Mario Balotelli. He was pulled over by police and they asked him why he had over 5,000 pound in the passenger seat and he simply replied “Because I’m rich”.

Saying “Because I’m Rich” if you are rich, must feel awesome!!

Lionel Andres “Leo” Messi is an Argentine footballer who plays as a forward for F.C. Barcelona and the Argentina national team, where he serves as the captain. He is known for his magisterial dribbling, where nobody can get the ball off of his foot, hence he “stays on the ball.” You stay on the ball by keeping your business associates and friends separate.

metadata.title: Rump Shaker
annotation:
Another video of Teddy riley discussing Pharrell Williams writing this rap verse for him:

https://youtu.be/U5MO3DbGg04?t=405

Little did we know at the time, but Pharrell Williams wrote this verse for Teddy Riley. Check out Teddy’s interview on the breakfast club speaking about how it went about.

http://youtu.be/f7B5pJXVpyk?t=35m20s

A clever play on words based on ‘trick or treating’ on Halloween, an annual custom where children dress up in costumes and tell their neighbors “Trick or treat!!” – meaning if you don’t give us something sweet, we’ll play a prank on you.

In this song, however, “trickin'” refers to teasing someone who wants to have sex with you (a ‘trick’ can mean a person who teases and doesn’t satisfy). “Treatin'” refers to “provid(ing) with enjoyment or gratification”. So he’s not teasing, he’s pleasing.

The second line changes up the definitions of those same words. Here, “treatin'” means “to provide with free food, drink, or entertainment”. And “trick” refers to a prostitute. So he’s bragging that he doesn’t have to buy nice things for every girl he pimps (in the previous line, he says the way she shakes her body makes him a whole lot of money).
These lyrics were originally harmonized by DeBarge in their hit “I Like It”, except the original last line is “…that shows how much you really care”

metadata.title: The Chaos Path
annotation: Possibly a reference to Revelation 2:5, “Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen, and repent, and do the first works; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will remove thy candlestick out of his place, except thou repent.” The candles all being blown out at once could signify the Rapture, or an otherwise removal of God’s remaining few from the Earth as wrath prepares itself to ensue.

Possibly a reference to Daniel 12:2, “And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.” It sounds like the narrator did not have a happy ending after going through the endtimes and was appointed to everlasting contempt.

This is possibly a reference to Matthew 24:29, “Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened”, about how, during the endtimes, the Sun will be darkened to signify the coming wrath of God. The rest of the song after this sign in the Sun is about chaos, fear, sorrow, and oblivion break out onto the Earth.

Oakland during the 90s' was fairly dangerous, in large part due to the effects of the war on drugs.

Armstrong is saying that he wants to avoid falling into the dangerous paths that the inner cities formed, such as intense drug use and alcoholism, along with the high levels of violent crime.

Even through all of that, Armstrong had to keep pushing.

metadata.title: Afternoon
annotation: His despondency is likely a result of heartbreak and missing someone. He can’t help but waste the days away.

This lyric describes what it feels like to be plagued by anxiety. The lyric is very vivid and helps the reader/listener easily imagine the feeling of anxiety rushing through his/her entire body.
Here, Trevor seems to highlight the genetic aspect of anxiety as he describes it as a part of his blood, but he also suggests the thought of anxiety being something essential to life.
Blood being a metaphor for anxiety is apt because anxiety manifests itself in many ways, but some ways are restlessness and pains. Thus, worries can literally be painful. Sometimes anxiety pain can start in the chest and spread, which would be alike the pumping of blood from the heart to other parts of the body.

Tying hands with rope is common imagery seen in situations with a prisoner, the rope being alike handcuffs. Thus, by saying he tied the rope, Trevor is saying that he himself put himself in this position of vulnerability and powerlessness. Although he wants to escape, he can’t because he would need someone else to undo the knots and set him free. He believes he has set himself up to only be liberated by someone else.
Perhaps he made a decision that created the situation he is now in with a (past) lover, and the question indicates that he is starting to question that decision or regret it.

Demons are a common name for one’s insecurities, thus here Trevor is personifying his worries by saying that one is roaming freely. The term “on the loose” suggests that the demon is supposed to be contained and under control, and right now it is potentially dangerously wandering around, or, in the case of this metaphor/personification, the worry is plaguing his thoughts and he can’t calm himself down. The head-hunter mentioned acts as a personification of the worry is preying upon his thoughts that won’t leave him alone.
This somewhat violent imagery connected with anxiety can be linked to something Trevor talked about in an interview with Music Feeds:

For an entire year I was worried I’d kill someone. It kind of obsessed my mind when it took me to my dark place, I’d have images flash in my mind of people I’d lost. A lot of the anxieties are like violence… just crazy things. You wrestle with things which aren’t real, your mind takes you to weird fucking places you don’t even think of.  And when it happens in real life, it’s even scarier.

When they’re speaking they get muddled with their words and maybe are afraid to say what they really mean. But singing provides a more open platform for them to express themselves and it’s a way for them to really express how they feel.

Youth Lagoon is portraying this sense of despondency and emotionless. A feeling of being distracted or out of place. We get this image of someone sitting inside a dark room all day watching TV without really seeing the images, this gives off a sense of depression or emptiness.

metadata.title: Plan to Be Surprised
annotation: It’s a cold night, and he merely wants to be let in; he knows they are home.

These lines seem rather creepy, but don’t be alarmed; based on not only the genre of music but the implication that this is directed at a past partner, he has likely made a promise to be there for them, and knows they are present at home. He knows that they’re afraid of also feeling like nothing, but he’s still there to help them not feel like nothing, even though they do it to him.
The narrator is going through an extremely difficult time, and the person this segment is directed at is making it worse by making him feel as though he’s nothing.

metadata.title: Wither
annotation: In many cases, depression comes without a defined catalyst and the sufferer of the disorder will try to rationalize their depression to a certain event or person.
Depression can cause people to change dramatically, to the point where they may not even recognize themselves.
There is a way for the writer to break free from depression; this could be taken as either committing suicide or taking the initiative to seek help.
Many depressed people sleep excessively. It is an activity in which they don’t have to think about their condition, and some argue that it simulates death.

annotation: Lomes is suggesting that the person leaving her has severely impacted her mental health. This person helped her stay mentally sound, and now that they’re not here anymore, she’s having problems keeping her emotional values in check.

metadata.title: Kodak
annotation:
Free cuts through all the bullshit, and calls out his rivals. He sees them for who they truly are, presumably inferior beings to himself.

Kodak is an American company who, at their peak, were almost synonymous with the home photography market. They ran an ad campaign back in the 80s that was backed by a choral version of Cyndi Lauper’s hit “True Colors”.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pGGyxt7ar8E

Bay Area rapper The Jacka was a friend of Freeway’s, the two of them even collaborated on a joint album together, Highway Robbery, in 2014.



Not long after this, in early 2015, The Jacka was sadly shot and killed in Oakland, California.

Freeway didn’t hide his sorrow about the passing of his friend and collaborator, and warns here that the people who did it can expect a similar fate by his hand if he comes across them.

Freeway and Beanie Sigel, both natives of Philadelphia, have a personal and professional relationship that goes back a long way.



Sigel hasn’t had the best time of it since his aforementioned prison release. Just a few months after getting out, in December of 2014, he was involved in an altercation that saw him shot in the abdomen and left needing surgery.

It was widely reported that the incident caused him to need one of his lungs removed, although reports also came out stating that wasn’t the case.

Regardless of the specifics, it obviously left him in a pretty bad way but, according to Freeway, Beans is back to full strength now and the two friends are ready to get back to work again.

State Property is the Philadelphia based Hip-Hop collective that Freeway is a member of.



A couple of the emcees on their roster have been released from jail since Freeway last put a record out, which he acknowledges here.

“O” would be Oschino, who was released in 2014 after serving a term behind bars. “Mac” refers to State Property’s head honcho, legendary Philadelphia emcee Beanie Sigel, who also got out in 2014 after serving 15 months for tax evasion.

metadata.title: Straight Edge Revenge
annotation:
John Porcelly is rather bluntly stating that he is a much stronger person than someone who is addicted to alcohol, cigarettes, and hard drugs.

There also seems to be a bit of a hip-hop influence in these lyrics as, in the same manner as “ego” rappers like LL Cool J and EPMD, Porcelly is claiming to be an equally, if not more, powerful force than the “chemical refreshments” non-straight-edge individuals are abusing, especially if he finds himself compelled to literally smack the living shit out of an alcoholic or drug abuser.

metadata.title: Walls Down
annotation: MEMBA came to me with the music video idea and at first i was worried tbh haha. If you know MEMBA you know that they take things to the next level with their crazy worlds and visuals. They wanted me to be a queen (which was fine with me..) on a thrown in a foreign made up world. But when they came to me with the masks they wanted me to wear I was pretty shocked hahah. So I did my research and we found the perfect fit. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Zs-N8RTmw0M
I was thinking of war when I wrote this song. Differing opinions, friction, boundary lines breaking down.
when i first heard the beat of this song I felt empowered, like a queen or king. There was something so badass about the feeling of the song. So i channeled that energy

metadata.title: The State-Lottery
annotation: The goose step is a special marching step which is performed during formal military parades and other ceremonies.

Social services are often farmed out to private concerns that make it more difficult to access said services.  The less the private industry provides to citizens, the more money they can keep for themselves.  The lines are especially poignant when one considers the American healthcare care system.
This doesn’t seem right; the people act like they’ve won the lottery with their new leader, but in fact, they’re just getting ready for more of the same old shit behind a new face.

Contrary to the more popular “Nation-States”, an attack on the one-percent, this song sets its sights on the sheep-like people who subscribe to the ideology pushed by the state. Chris Hannah questions the excitement displayed upon the inauguration of a new President or Prime Minister.

The song opens with an excerpt from “Noam Chomsky’s “Chomsky on Democracy and Education.” This reading sets the tone for Propagandhi’s attack on what we view as democracy, which is actually (according to Chomsky) far from it.

metadata.title: Kick the Chair
annotation: The 24 hour news cycle is always looking for the next big topic, the next victim they can shout about, the next person they can tear down… right or wrong.

Hangings in the old west are popularly depicted with the person to be hanged standing on a stool or chair, with the rope tied to a sturdy tree limb. The rope would be pulled tight, then the chair kicked out from under the convict.

A twisting of the biblical phrase “the way the truth and the life.”

Jesus told Thomas that he, Jesus, was the way, the truth, and the life, meaning that he was the model for making it to heaven.

Dave Mustaine here is twisting that meaning to imply that the court is corrupt. It could also be drawing a literal distinction between truths and lies being told under oath.
